issues.description: External function 'exit_func' parameter usage is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement (problem_statement.md) explicitly requires calling an external function exit_func with an integer status code. The template (template_repository/helloWorld.asm) does not declare or call exit_func (it only declares 'extern printf'), so students are not shown the external symbol to use. The reference solution (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm) declares 'extern exit_func' (line 8) and calls it (line 18) but does not push or otherwise pass the required integer status code before the call. This leaves students without a consistent, correct example of how to satisfy the requirement and produces a reference implementation that does not demonstrate the required parameter passing.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the artifacts consistent and demonstrate correct parameter passing. In the template, add the extern declaration for the required external symbol (e.g. add the line 'extern exit_func' near the other externs) so students see the symbol to call. In the solution, pass an integer status code according to the calling convention before calling exit_func (for example: 'push dword 0' or 'push 0' immediately before 'call exit_func') or document an alternative parameter-passing mechanism if intended. Update the problem statement or comments to explicitly show the expected status value and calling convention to avoid ambiguity.
